blocks.text: Setting up your Notion workspace for community growth

Building a community requires a central source of truth. Your Notion workspace acts as your home base for member data and content strategy. Start by creating a main dashboard page. Use a database to house your member list. Add properties for joining date, member tier, and last interaction. This helps you track engagement at a glance.
Using keyboard shortcuts to move faster

Efficiency comes from keeping your hands on the keyboard. Notion supports standard Mac shortcuts. Use ⌘ P to open the search bar instantly. Type / to open the block menu and pick from text, headers, or lists. If you forget a shortcut, press ⇧ ? to see the full list. Lazur can also point out where specific menu items live if you get stuck.

items: ⌘ ⇧ N: Open a new Notion window.
⌘ [ and ⌘ ]: Navigate back or forward in history.

blocks.text: Community builders often juggle multiple event calendars. Create a database for your events and use a Calendar view. Add a property for status, such as Planned, Announced, or Completed. This view gives you a clear visual of your upcoming schedule. You can filter this view to show only events for the current month.
If you struggle to find a specific filter, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where the filter button is. It will circle the correct icon on your screen so you do not have to hunt for it.
blocks.title: Find buttons with Lazur

blocks.text: Onboarding is your first impression. Build a template in your member database. Include a checklist of welcome steps. Use headings to break up long instructions. Add a callout block to highlight important links or community rules. This ensures every new member gets the same high quality experience.
Common mistakes in Notion workspace design

Many builders clutter their sidebar with too many top level pages. Use sub pages to keep things organized. Another mistake is using too many databases. Start simple. Combine related information into one database with different views. This makes maintenance much easier as your community grows.
Keeping your data secure and accessible

Permissions matter when you work with a team. Click the Share button at the top right to manage access. Use the granular settings to control who can edit or comment. Regularly review your shared pages to ensure only the right people have access to sensitive member data.
What to do next with your community hub

Refine your workspace as your needs evolve. Add a table of contents to long pages. Use formulas to calculate member tenure automatically. If you ever feel overwhelmed by the interface, remember that Lazur is there to help. Just hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask a question or get guidance on a specific feature.

faq.question: Does Notion work offline on Mac?
faq.answer: Notion requires an internet connection to sync changes. You can view cached pages offline, but you cannot edit them effectively.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to automate my Notion tasks?
faq.answer: Lazur does not click buttons for you. It points at items, explains features, and guides you through steps so you can do the work yourself.

faq.question: What is the best way to organize a large community workspace?
faq.answer: Use a clear hierarchy of parent pages and sub pages. Keep your main dashboard clean and use database views to hide clutter.

faq.question: How do I check if my Mac supports the latest Notion app?
faq.answer: Notion requires macOS 13 or later. You can check your version in the Apple menu > About This Mac.
